// why: This file is the project's. Herdr wrote a first version and never replaces
one that exists. `npm run typecheck` and the editor both read it.
gpui-kit.d.ts beside it is Herdr's: generated, never edited, not in git.
`target` and `module`: the files are ES2022 modules, and Herdr loads them
`moduleResolution`: left out, an ES module project gets the legacy
resolution, which never looks in node_modules.
`lib`: ES2022 without the browser's globals. This runtime is not a
browser, and gpui-kit.d.ts declares the globals it does have (`console`,
`fetch`, `localStorage`): the browser's declarations collide with them.
`checkJs`: the mod is plain JavaScript, typed through JSDoc comments and
types.d.ts. Without it nothing here is checked.
`strict`: all of it, null checks included. A value that can be null or
undefined is typed so, and handled where it is used.
`strictPropertyInitialization` is the one strict check left off, for the
view in main.js. Herdr builds a view through `init`, not a constructor, so
its field (`part`) cannot be assigned where this check looks. Every other
class assigns its fields in its constructor and passes with the check on.
`noEmit`: the check only reads, nothing is built.
